## Why

Users of `beta` want a greeting on start-up, and the text belongs in `alpha`,
the shared library, so that other tools can use it too.

## Scope

In: the greeting text in `alpha`; printing it in `beta`.

Out: translations; any change to `gamma`.

## Requirements

### R1 Greeting text
`alpha` SHALL provide the greeting `hello, demo` for a caller that asks for it.

#### R1.S1 Default greeting
- GIVEN `alpha` at the branch head
- WHEN a caller asks for the greeting with no name
- THEN it gets the exact text `hello, demo` (11 characters, no trailing
  newline)

#### R1.S2 Name too long
- GIVEN a name of 65 characters
- WHEN a caller asks for the greeting with that name
- THEN it gets an error naming the 64-character limit, and no greeting

### R2 beta prints the greeting
`beta` SHALL print the greeting from `alpha` as its first line of output.

#### R2.S1 Start-up line
- GIVEN `beta` built against `alpha` at the branch head
- WHEN `beta` starts with no arguments
- THEN its first line of standard output is `hello, demo`, within 1 s of
  start (wall time)

## Approaches

1. Greeting in `alpha`, printed by `beta` (picked: one source of the text).
2. Greeting in `beta` only (rejected: other tools would copy the text).

## Open calls

1. The name limit is 64 characters, counted as Unicode code points.

39	- emits the §5 frontmatter (with `project:` as the line after `timeout_min:`
40	  when `--project` is given, and no `project:` line otherwise) and places each
41	  file in the right queue;
42	- **scope-commits only the files it wrote** (never `git add -A`), with a plain-text
43	  message, and pushes with up to 3 pull-rebase retries.
44	
45	## Do this
46	
47	1. Write the body to a temp file (e.g. `/tmp/mesh-post-body.md`). Make it
48	   self-contained; when fanning out to different OSes/nodes, write one body per
49	   variant and call the script once per variant.
50	2. Run the script:
51	
52	```bash
53	<repo>/product/skills/mesh-post/mesh-post.sh \
54	  --to role:build --to role:geworker \
55	  --type task.request --title trilinos-spack-build \
56	  --priority normal --timeout-min 300 \
57	  --body-file /tmp/mesh-post-body.md
58	```
59	
60	   Flags: `--to` (repeatable) is `role:<role>` or a bare `<agent_id>`; `--type` is
61	   `task.request` | `query` | `reply` | `task.cancel` | `library.submit` | …;
62	   `--title` is a kebab-case slug; optional `--priority low|normal|high` (default
63	   normal), `--timeout-min N` (default 120), `--credentials K1,K2` (KEY NAMES only,
64	   never values), `--depends-on id1,id2`, `--project proj:<name>`, `--from <id>`,
65	   `--repo <path>`. Add `--dry-run` to write + stage without commit/push when you
66	   want to inspect first.
67	
68	3. Report to the user in one line per target: the target, the assigned id, and the
69	   file path — and that they will see the outcome (status/reply) on their next
70	   CHECK of the ledger. You do NOT wait here; the claiming node's poller senses the
71	   message on its next scan and routes any `reply` into your inbox
72	   (`tasks/<from-id>/`).
73	
74	## Notes
75	
76	- **`--project` loads a project space for the executor.** Give it when the task
77	  works in a project memory space: `--project proj:<name>`, matching
78	  `^proj:[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$`. The claiming node loads that space for its
79	  executor (PROTOCOL §5, `spec/memory-spaces.md` §5). The script checks the
80	  value while it reads its arguments, before it looks at the repo, so an
81	  invalid value exits 1 with `mesh-post: invalid --project value: <value>` and
82	  writes no message. The space must be mounted on the bus (`spaces.yaml`);
83	  posting does not check that, and a claiming node that cannot find it blocks
84	  the task.
85	- **Type tells the consumer what it is.** `task.request`/`query`/`task.cancel` are
86	  claimable work (get a `status/<id>.json`); `library.submit` is drained by the
87	  librarian and gets no status; `reply` is information the recipient just surfaces.
88	- **Unstaffed role is fine.** Posting to a role no node currently holds just waits
89	  until one comes online. To check who holds a role:
90	  `grep -l "<role>" <repo>/agents/*.yaml`.
91	- **Git gate.** The script uses the literal `-C <repo>` form and a plain-text commit
92	  message, staging only its new files, so it stays inside the node git gate.
93	  Invoking mesh-post authorizes that one scoped commit+push — that is the skill's
94	  job; it does not touch the working tree's other changes.

1	---
2	name: space-librarian
3	description: File records into a memory space (a Project Space or any other rw space) after the header-profile, reference and id checks, one commit per record, pushed to the space's main. Invoke when a librarian node files records into a space that spaces.yaml assigns to its role, when a session with no bus files a record into a space checkout, or when someone asks to file, check or desk-run records for a space.
4	allowed-tools: Read, Write, Bash, Grep, Glob
5	---
6	
7	# space-librarian: file records into a memory space
8	
9	A memory space (the memory-spaces design) is a git repo of records with one
10	writer per mesh, its librarian. This skill is that writer. It is given a space
11	root and record files, checks each record, and files the ones that pass: one
12	commit per record, pushed to the space's `main`. It needs no bus.
13	
14	## Who runs it
15	
16	- **On a mesh.** A mesh librarian uses this skill for every rw space that
17	  `spaces.yaml` assigns to its role: each entry with `access: rw` and its role
18	  in `librarian:`. It never writes a space listed `access: ro`. To list the
19	  spaces a role files (one-line entries, as the registry is written):
20	
21	  ```sh
22	  grep -E 'access:[[:space:]]*rw' <bus root>/spaces.yaml |
23	    grep -E 'librarian:[[:space:]]*<role>[[:space:]]*[},]'
24	  ```
25	
26	- **Without a bus** (single seat). The session uses this skill directly, on
27	  its checkout of the space, as its own librarian. The checks are the same;
28	  the real values they look for then come from the node alone.
29	
30	It files what it is handed. Deciding what belongs in the space, and who may
31	hand it over, is the caller's job.
32	
33	## Inputs
34	
35	- **Space root**: the space's checkout, a git repo with `space.yaml` at its
36	  root and the space's remote as `origin`. In a bus it is `spaces/<path>`.
37	- **Records**: paths relative to the space root, each already written at that
38	  path. They are checked, and filed, in the order given.
39	- **Bus root** (optional). If not given, the bus is the space's superproject,
40	  else the `REPO_PATH` in `~/.agent-identity.env`. It counts only if it has
41	  `agents/`. With none, there is no bus.
42	
43	## Output
44	
45	One line per record, in the order given, and nothing else:
46	
47	```
48	FILED <space path> <sha7>
49	REFUSED <space path>: <profile|reference|id> line <n>
50	```
51	
52	`<n>` is the 1-based line of the record where the check failed. The checks run
53	in the order profile, reference, id, and the first that fails is reported, at
54	its first failing line. The output never holds the matched text or any value
55	the checks search for. A record path that names no file is an error for the
56	caller, not a result line.
57	
58	## 1. Check each record
59	
60	The three checks, as the script below runs them:
61	
62	- **profile.** No real hostname, agent id, mesh task id or credential key
63	  name, and no home path, anywhere in the file. Real values come from the bus
64	  where one is present: `agents/*.yaml` (`agent_id`, `agent_name`,
65	  `hostname` and its first label, `credentials_available`, `cwd`), the
66	  direct-inbox names under `tasks/`, and the task ids in the file names under
67	  `tasks/`, `status/` and `_archive/`. From the node come the local hostname
68	  (`hostname` and `uname -n`, with their first labels) and the credential key
69	  names in `~/.agent-credentials.env`. Home paths are matched by four
70	  patterns:
71	  - the local `$HOME`;
72	  - each registered agent's `cwd`;
73	  - the first two path components of each registered agent's `cwd`;
74	  - absolute per-user paths under the macOS and Linux home roots.
75	
76	  Generic `~/` paths are allowed, and so is an id-shaped example that no bus
77	  holds. Values shorter than three characters are skipped. Each value
78	  matches as a whole word. A hostname or credential key name inside a longer
79	  name joined by `-` or `_` passes. An agent id, agent name or task id joined
80	  that way does not, as in the bus's own `<task id>-<slug>` file names.
81	- **reference** (Markdown records). Every citation must resolve. A citation
82	  is a value of a front-matter reference field (`related`, `supersedes`,
83	  `superseded_by`, `discovered_in`), or a qualified cross-space id
84	  `<space id>/<record id>` in the body outside inline code and fenced blocks,
85	  where a space id is `core`, `lore`, `lore:<name>` or `proj:<name>`. A
86	  trailing `@<commit>` pin is ignored. It resolves when it is:
87	  - a URL;
88	  - a record id held by a record in the space (in its `id:` line, or as the
89	    start of its file name);
90	  - a qualified id whose space is listed in `may_reference` in `space.yaml`,
91	    or is this space (then the rest must resolve here);
92	  - a change id with a folder `changes/<id>/` or
93	    `changes/archive/<date>-<id>/`;
94	  - `<change>/T<n>`, where that change's `plan.md` has task `T<n>` as a
95	    heading or a table row.
96	- **id** (Markdown records). The id is the front-matter `id:`; under
97	  `decisions/` and `handoffs/` with no `id:` line it is the file name. A
98	  record with no id passes. An id already at this same path on `origin/main`
99	  (or `HEAD`, where there is no `origin/main`) is not new and passes. A new
100	  id must have the form
101	  `<category>-<YYYYMMDDTHHMMZ>-<4 hex>`, or the UTC-named form: `ev-<UTC>`,
102	  or `ev-<UTC>-<shard id>` for a shard (a task id and one lowercase letter),
103	  such as `ev-<UTC>-T19a`, under `changes/<id>/evidence/`; `<UTC>-<slug>`
104	  under `decisions/` and `handoffs/`. It must not be already present: no
105	  other file in the space holds it. Evidence, decisions and handoffs are one
106	  file per event, so a record there whose path is already on `origin/main`
107	  with other content is refused as `id`.
108	
109	Copy the script into a file in a scratch directory outside the space, never
110	inside it, and run it with `sh`:
111	
112	```
113	SPACE=<space root> sh <script file> <space path> ...
114	```
115	
116	Set `BUS=<bus root>` to name the bus. It prints `REFUSED ...` for a record
117	that fails, and `CHECKED <space path>` for one that passes. `CHECKED` is a
118	working line: those records go on to section 2, and it is never part of the
119	output. The script is POSIX `sh`, and its patterns are `grep -E`, `sed -E`
120	and POSIX `awk` (no `grep -P`, no GNU-only flag), so it runs unchanged with
121	BSD and GNU tools. The value lists it builds stay in its own temporary
122	directory, which it deletes on exit.
123	
124	```sh
125	: "${SPACE:?set SPACE to the space root}"
126	SPACE=${SPACE%/}
127	W=$(mktemp -d) || exit 2
128	trap 'rm -rf "$W"' EXIT
129	esc() { sed -e 's#[[\.*^$+?(){}|]#\\&#g'; }
130	val() { sed -n -E "s/^$1:[[:space:]]*\"?([^\"#[:space:]]+).*/\\1/p" "$2"; }
131	
132	# The bus: given, else the space's superproject, else the node's REPO_PATH.
133	if [ -z "${BUS:-}" ]; then
134	  BUS=$(git -C "$SPACE" rev-parse --show-superproject-working-tree 2>/dev/null)
135	  [ -n "$BUS" ] && [ -d "$BUS/agents" ] || BUS=
136	  if [ -z "$BUS" ] && [ -f "$HOME/.agent-identity.env" ]; then
137	    BUS=$(sed -n -E 's/^REPO_PATH=["]?([^"#[:space:]]+).*/\1/p' \
138	      "$HOME/.agent-identity.env" | head -n 1)
139	  fi
140	fi
141	[ -n "$BUS" ] && [ -d "$BUS/agents" ] || BUS=

143	# profile: real values from the bus and the node, built at run time, in three
144	# lists by boundary: words (hostnames, credential key names), agents (agent
145	# ids and names, inbox names) and tids (mesh task ids).

147	if [ -n "$BUS" ]; then

173	# A value matches as a whole word. In words, `-` and `_` are word characters,
174	# so a label inside a longer name passes. Agent ids and task ids end at any
175	# non-alphanumeric character, so `node-<agent id>` and the bus's own
176	# `<task id>-<slug>` names match, and a task id also ends at a letter.
177	pat() {  # list $1, left boundary class $2, right boundary class $3
178	  sed -E 's/^[[:space:]"]+//; s/[[:space:]"]+$//' "$W/$1" |
179	    grep -E '^.{3,}$' | grep -vE '^(null|~)$' | sort -u | esc |

181	}

183	  pat tids A-Za-z0-9 0-9; } > "$W/profile"
184	sed -E 's#/+$##' "$W/paths" | grep -E '^/.{2,}' | sort -u | esc |
185	  sed 's#.*#&([^A-Za-z0-9_.-]|$)#' >> "$W/profile"
186	printf '%s\n' '(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_.-])/(Users|home)/[A-Za-z0-9._-]+' >> "$W/profile"
187	
188	# reference: this space's id and its may_reference list.
189	SID=$(val id "$SPACE/space.yaml" | head -n 1)
190	awk '/^may_reference:/ {
191	       s = $0; sub(/^may_reference:[ \t]*/, "", s); sub(/[ \t]*#.*$/, "", s)

201	idof() {  # "<line> <id>" from a record's front-matter on stdin

204	       /^id:/ { x = $0; sub(/^id:[ \t]*/, "", x); sub(/[ \t]+#.*$/, "", x)

239	refs() {  # "<line> <citation>" for each citation in record $1
240	  awk 'function emit(x) { gsub(/^[ \t"]+|[ \t"]+$/, "", x)
241	                          if (x != "" && x != "null" && x != "~") print NR, x }
242	       NR == 1 { if ($0 != "---") exit; next }
243	       $0 == "---" { exit }
244	       /^(related|supersedes|superseded_by|discovered_in):/ {
245	         x = $0; sub(/^[a-z_]+:/, "", x); sub(/[ \t]+#.*$/, "", x)
246	         blk = (x ~ /^[ \t]*$/); gsub(/\[|\]/, "", x)
247	         n = split(x, a, ","); for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) emit(a[i]); next }
248	       blk && /^[ \t]+-[ \t]/ { x = $0; sub(/^[ \t]+-[ \t]+/, "", x)
249	                                sub(/[ \t]+#.*$/, "", x); emit(x); next }
250	       { blk = 0 }' "$1"
251	  awk 'NR == 1 && $0 == "---" { fm = 1; print ""; next }
252	       fm { if ($0 == "---") fm = 0; print ""; next }
253	       /^[ \t]*(```|~~~)/ { fence = !fence; print ""; next }
254	       fence { print ""; next }
255	       /^[ \t]*$/ { code = 0 }
256	       { out = ""; s = $0
257	         while ((i = index(s, "`")) > 0) {
258	           if (!code) out = out substr(s, 1, i - 1)
259	           code = !code; s = substr(s, i + 1) }
260	         if (!code) out = out s
261	         print out }' "$1" |
262	    grep -noE "$QID" | sed -E 's/^([0-9]+):[^a-z]?/\1 /'

265	BASE=HEAD
266	if git -C "$SPACE" rev-parse -q --verify origin/main >/dev/null 2>&1; then

270	  r=${r#./}; f=$SPACE/$r
271	  if [ ! -f "$f" ]; then echo "no such record: $r" >&2; continue; fi

280	  if [ -n "$n" ]; then echo "REFUSED $r: reference line $n"; continue; fi
281	  # id

283	  if [ -z "$x" ]; then
284	    case "$r" in
285	      decisions/*.md|handoffs/*.md) id=$(basename "$r" .md); n=1 ;;

287	  fi
288	  if [ -n "$id" ]; then

292	        form="$form|ev-[0-9]{8}T[0-9]{4}Z(-T[0-9]+[a-z])?" ;;

294	        form="$form|[0-9]{8}T[0-9]{4}Z-[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*" ;;

299	          { echo "REFUSED $r: id line $n"; continue; }
